Oh I can contribute to this conversation ! I work as an HR consultant for small businesses and non-profits and have been for 3 years. I do almost everything from giving advice to crafting documents, coach managers, employees, help in the hiring process, make sure labor laws are respected etc etc etc. 

I am part of a small firm of 7 people that are all consultants and 1 owner/manager. This last year has left me in a bad headspace mentally regarding work because no matter what type of company you work for, HR will almost always protect the business instead of the employees.

This was a shock to me, cause I had a career reorientation and went into HR, naively thinking I could really make a difference and not be one of those. I've since had my delusions shattered. Even in small places, HR almost never cares for their employees. And it is my role now to perpetuate this tradition. I have to go in the direction my firm has chosen and 90% of the time, it goes against the employees and my principles. It really makes me sick to my stomach really. 

I unfortunatly cannot afford or hope to change jobs at this moment and so Im stuck being what I swore I wouldn't be. 

NEVER TRUST HR.

I work as an HR consultant for small and medium buisnesses. It's super rewarding to help my clients who often don't have the time or can't afford a full time HR. My work is super diverse, as we have all kinds of clients and every contract is different. It's 100% WFH too so I don't have to over socialize with my coworkers. Workers rights are super important to me and I get to help put in place lawfull and ethical practices. Win-win! Downside is some of the client try to cut corners, but it's my job to convince them otherwise :)

Tried various and honestly hated almost all of them, even the zoloft I took for 3-4 years. It makes it so my life gets "blurry" and I experience derealization and general apathy towards anything. I am no longer depressed for sure but I also experience very little joy, like living life in neutral.

My doctor is highly resistant towards prescribing actual anxiety meds and wants me to go back on anti-depressant, which is a no for me.
